On the surface, it is tempting to speculate that the lack of a relaxation phase in the slow cadence condition positively mediated results, perhaps via effects associated with increased ischemia and hypoxia. However, the fact that other aspects of the study were not controlled (i.e., concentric and eccentric tempo, intensity of load) clouds the ability to draw firm conclusions on the topic.
